In the past year, new specifications covering source adaptation and support for WireGuard virtual private network (VPN) have been published. RIST support has been added to OBS (ver. 27.2), VLC (ver. 3.0.12), as well as continuing support in FFmpeg and other open-source projects such as TSDuck. Work continues by the RIST Activity Group within the Video Service Forum (VSF) toward other enhanced capabilities for RIST, including support for hybrid satellite/internet delivery and advanced firewall traversal support known as RIST relay (which is about to be published). The RIST AG is co-chaired by Rick Ackermans of CBS Operations and Engineering and Wes Simpson of LearnIPvideo.com. Ground–Cloud–Cloud–Ground (GCCG). This activity group has been collecting and organizing user requirements and works toward establishing a common technical approach such that multivendor interoperation VSF Current Activity Groups/Standards Development The Reliable Internet Stream Transport (RIST) project was created to be the first completely open specification for delivering high-quality, low-latency, professional media streams over the public internet. A range of technologies are supported in RIST such as automatic repeat reQuest (ARQ), forward error correction (FEC), and encryption using a choice of datagram transport layer security (DTLS) and phase-shift keying (PSK). RIST also supports multiple network configurations including multilink bonding, stream striping, and hitless protection switching. Three profiles of RIST have been published to date: simple, main, and advanced (resp. TR-06-1, -2, and -3).
